narrative: The model estimated a 27.0% probability that you would become a bad credit risk. Although that may not sound very high, it was above the bank’s cutoff for this application, so you were classified as a bad risk and the loan was denied. The strongest influence was your savings profile: you have no known savings or unspecified savings. This factor actually worked in your favor and lowered the risk estimate, but it was not enough to offset the overall picture. The second most influential factor was that you already have another installment plan with a bank. Only about 8.7% of approved applicants have this, and it pushed the assessment toward bad credit because it adds another regular repayment obligation. Third, the loan purpose—a used car—modestly reduced the risk estimate; used-car requests make up about 13.6% of approved applicants. Other details also matter in the full assessment, such as your requested amount being much higher than the approved average and a history of past delays. To improve future chances, reduce existing installment obligations, build a documented savings record, and consider requesting a smaller amount. You may also ask the bank whether correcting or supplementing your savings information could support reconsideration.
